verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is designed to last approximately 10 days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "10-day mission" (R1); "about a 10-day mission" (R2); "approximately 10-day Artemis II mission" (R3); "10-day journey" (R4); "approximately 10 days" (R5); "10-day journey" (R6); "10-day expedition" (R7); "10-day mission" (R9); "10-day Artemis II journey" (R10)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state the mission duration as approximately 10 days.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission launches on April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "blasted off... on Wednesday evening" dated 2026/04/01 (R1); launch at 6:35 p.m. EDT April 1 (R3); "April 1" (R4, R5); "April 1, 2026" (R7, R9)
verifications.reasoning: Sources consistently report launch on April 1, 2026.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission has a four-person crew.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "four astronauts" (R1, R2, R6); "four crew members" (R3); "four-person Artemis II crew" (R4); "four members" (R5); "crew of four" (R7); "crew of four astronauts" (R9, R10)
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm exactly four crew members.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission crew will journey around the Moon and return to Earth.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "journey around the moon but not land there" (R1); "around the Moon and back" (R2, R3); "around the far side of the moon and back" (R4); "flyby... circle it, and begin the return" (R5); "around the moon and back" (R7); "around the Moon and back to Earth" (R9); "looping around the moon’s far side before returning to Earth" (R10)
verifications.reasoning: Directly supported by mission descriptions in sources.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission crew will test the Orion spacecraft's systems before splashdown in the Pacific Ocean.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "splashdown in the Pacific Ocean on April 10"; tests in orbit, toward moon (R1); "splashdown in the Pacific Ocean"; "test life support systems" (R7); "splash down... off the coast of San Diego" after tests (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm Pacific splashdown and system tests throughout mission prior to it.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission type is crewed lunar flyby.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "around the moon but not land" crewed (R1); "crewed mission to lunar orbit... flyby" (R5); "lunar flyby mission" (R7); "lunar flyby" (R9); "lunar flyby" (R10)
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly described as crewed lunar flyby without landing.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission has no lunar landing.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "not land there" (R1); "will not land on the moon" (R4, R5); "will not land on the moon" (R7, R9); "will not land on the moon" (R10)

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission length is ~10 days (approx. 240 hours).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: ~10 days throughout, e.g., "10-day mission" (R1-R9); 10 days = 240 hours

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission crew will test systems in high Earth orbit.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission crew will journey toward the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "path toward the moon" (R1); "journey to the moon" (R2-R5, R7, R9)

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission crew will fly by the lunar far side around day 5-6.
verifications.label: CLEAR

verifications.label: CLEAR

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is the first crewed flight of the SLS rocket.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "pave the way to land... on Artemis III" (R2); "essential preparatory work for... Artemis III" landing (R4); "paving the way for future lunar landings" (R5); "pave the way for Artemis III" (R10)
